summary: Colusa County state fire lookout west of Williams, built 1931 and staffed by O. W. Friedrick; FFLA lists it as gone and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Lookout house on Three Sisters Peak; FFLA lists the type as Ground
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; no source gives a removal date or describes the site now
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry (page header and December 1930 notices)

events.note: State agreed to a station in December 1930; lookout house being built by April 1931 with local stockmen
O. W. Friedrick in charge of the lookout by May 1931
Road to the station being built by November 1931; before it, travel was difficult with nothing but a trail
May 29, 1931: Friedrick phoned the Colusa fire house about smoke; it was weeds burning in town
May 1932 notice that Friedrick would begin his summer's work as lookout, unless something unforeseen developed; road open and public invited to inspect the station

evidence.supports: State Forester M. B. Pratt accepted Colusa County's proposal for a fire lookout station in Colusa County (December 22, 1930 item)
evidence.quote: State Forester M. B. Pratt, attending the Northern California Fireman's Association which met here yesterday, accepted Colusa County's proposition to establish a fire lookout station in Colusa County

evidence.supports: A site was selected and a roadway provided for by late December 1930
evidence.quote: a site had been selected and the construction of a suitable roadway to the building had been provided for

evidence.supports: State to furnish the lookout man
evidence.quote: The state will furnish the man to assume the duties of lookout.

evidence.supports: Lookout house being built by April 1931 (April 4, 1931 item) in cooperation with stockmen
evidence.quote: A lookout house is being built on Three Sisters Peak west of Williams in co-operation with the stockmen in that vicinity.

evidence.supports: Before the road, travel to the station was difficult, with nothing but a trail
evidence.quote: It has been difficult to travel to and from the lookout with nothing but a trail.

evidence.supports: Road to the station being built in November 1931 (November 2, 1931 item)
evidence.quote: a road is being built to Three Sisters lookout station west of Williams

evidence.supports: O. W. Friedrick in charge of the lookout in 1931
evidence.quote: in charge of the forest service lookout recently established on Three Sisters Mountain, west of Williams

evidence.supports: Station connected by telephone to the state ranger's office in Williams
evidence.quote: The lookout station is connected with the state ranger's office in Williams by telephone

evidence.supports: Friedrick to begin the 1932 summer season, unless something unforeseen develops (May 27, 1932 item)
evidence.quote: unless something unforeseen develops, O.W. Friedrick of Little Valley will begin his summer's work as lookout at Three Sisters, west of Williams.

evidence.supports: Page header lists the station under the California Department of Forestry
evidence.quote: Colusa County - California Dept. of Forestry

evidence.supports: Friedrick phoned the Colusa fire house about smoke on May 29, 1931
evidence.quote: told Percy Cooks at the local fire house in a telephone call this morning at 10:30 o'clock

evidence.supports: The smoke was weeds burning in town, not a fire
evidence.quote: the smoke was merely that coming from weeds which city employes were burning in the residential part of town

evidence.supports: Local paper said the episode showed the lookout was worth having
evidence.quote: the lookout on Three Sisters is valuable

evidence.supports: Road open and public invited to inspect the station (May 27, 1932 item)
evidence.quote: 'The road to the lookout station is open,' Wilcher said, 'and the public is invited to inspect the plant there.'

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Three Sisters in Colusa County as ground-type and gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The page header and December 1930 notices describe a state (California Department of Forestry) station, but a May 29, 1931 Colusa Herald item calls it a forest service lookout. The story says the sources disagree and does not settle it.

notes_for_editor: Built and staffing dates rest on 1930-1932 newspaper clippings as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. The FFLA county list prints FFLOS US 1872, CA 67 on the row before Three Sisters; in the firetower.org list that number belongs to Three Peaks Lookout Site, so it is not attached here. No removal date or site description found; a Colusa County or Colusa Herald archive search would be the next step. An earlier draft named a site author; the cached page text does not name one, so the source no longer does.
